subtopics.title: The Four Core Regions and the Prescribed Two

questions.question: The four core industrial regions of South Africa are:
options: Gauteng (PWV), Durban–Pinetown, Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage, South-Western Cape

questions.question: The organising sentence for the four regions is:
options: Minerals made Gauteng; harbours made the coastal three
Farming made the inland one; fishing made the rest

questions.question: The four rows of the case study exam grid are:
options: Location factors; main activities; success and hindering factors; economic and social impacts

subtopics.title: Gauteng — the PWV: South Africa's Industrial Heart

questions.question: PWV stands for:
Gauteng's water weakness was engineered away by:
options: The Vaal Dam and the Lesotho Highlands water scheme

questions.question: "Industrial regions outlive their reasons" refers to Gauteng because:
options: The region has closed most factories
Gold is nearly finished but the infrastructure, skills and market it assembled keep the region dominant

questions.question: Gauteng's chief locational handicap is:
options: No port — exports pay the overland leg to Durban

subtopics.title: Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage: The Motor Town on Algoa Bay

questions.question: The vehicle maker anchoring Kariega (Uitenhage) is:
The components speciality linking this region to the platinum case study is:
The region's structural weakness is:
options: Dependence on one industry — the motor sector

questions.question: The modern deep-water port serving the region is:

subtopics.title: Spreading the Map: SDIs, Corridors, IDZs and SEZs

questions.question: The flagship Spatial Development Initiative is the:
options: Maputo Development Corridor from Gauteng through Mpumalanga to Maputo

questions.question: The IDZ recipe is:
options: A serviced industrial estate at a port or airport with incentives, duty-free inputs for export production and one-stop services
A farming cooperative with state marketing

questions.question: Which pairing of zone and speciality is correct?
options: Richards Bay — minerals and metals beside the bulk port
East London — oil and gas only

questions.question: The balanced verdict on SDIs and IDZs is that they:
options: Have completely broken the four-region pattern
Have created no jobs at all
Redirect some growth but have not yet broken the four-region concentration

subtopics.title: Four Kitchens Cooking for One Country

questions.question: In the house picture, over-concentration means:
options: Four crowded, overheated kitchens while the other rooms sit cold and empty of work
Too many cooks in one kitchen

questions.question: The South-Western Cape kitchen mainly cooks:
options: Food, wine, clothing and printing for its comfortable market

questions.question: The four pocket questions for any case study are:
options: Why there, what do they cook, what helps and hurts, who eats

subtopics.title: The Kitchen With No Tap and No Door

questions.question: Gauteng is "the kitchen with no tap" because:
options: Its water is pumped in from the Vaal Dam and Lesotho's mountains

questions.question: "The giant outlived the gold that made it" because Gauteng still holds:
options: The converging railways, the skills, the biggest market and thousands of linked firms
Most of the world's unmined gold
The only harbour in the country

questions.question: "Gauteng is the factory and the office at once" refers to:
options: Heavy industry plus the continent's densest banks and head offices

questions.question: The standard image for Gauteng's social inequality is:
options: Sandton's towers across the highway from Alexandra

subtopics.title: The Car Town, and Lighting Stoves in the Cold Rooms

questions.question: The car town's six-word location story is:
options: Gold, coal, water, rail, market, skills
Port, rail, chosen by car makers
Sun, soil, rain, cane, mill, ship
Border, bridge, pass, gate, road, town

questions.question: "When the world stops buying cars, the whole town holds its breath" describes:
An IDZ as "a fully furnished flat for industry" means:
options: Ready infrastructure, services and incentives so export factories can move straight in

questions.question: The honest verdict on the new stoves is:
options: Partly working — real factories and jobs at Coega and East London, but the four kitchens still dominate
Fully successful — industry is now evenly spread
Total failure — no jobs created anywhere
Unknown — no zones have opened yet
